briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Demand Holds, Deals Heat Up: MI Weed Finds Its Footing as Rescheduling Fight Grinds On
briefs.top: Michigan operators are leaning into growth — a Detroit-born flower brand just cracked 90 stores and House of Dank keeps opening doors — even as the 24% wholesale tax squeezes margins and fuels a governor's-race promise to roll it back. Nationally, cannabis M&A is accelerating (Cronos just closed a European buy) and Compass Pathways says its psilocybin therapy is on track for an early-2027 launch, even as the DEA rescheduling case stays technically paused, not dead.

local.text: Detroit's Zasso scales to 90 Michigan stores — A small Detroit cultivation outfit selling top-shelf flower for about $100 an ounce hit shelves about a year ago and is now stocked in roughly 90 stores statewide, with most retailers reaching out first.
House of Dank opens new Berkley storefront — Michigan's leading cannabis retailer kept its statewide expansion rolling with a new Woodward-corridor location in Berkley.

Demand stays near all-time highs despite the tax — Consumer demand for regulated cannabis remains near a record even as low prices and the new wholesale tax push more operators toward consolidation, with dispensaries still on pace to sell over 1.3 million pounds of flower this year.

GOP governor nominee vows to gut the 24% tax — John James has pledged to repeal or sharply cut the wholesale tax, calling it a driver of higher prices and a boost to illegal operators, and industry executives have backed his campaign with real money this cycle.

Lansing lawmakers push bipartisan repeal bills — Legislators in both chambers have introduced bills to kill the controversial 24% wholesale tax as sales dip and businesses close, giving operators a legislative path forward alongside the pending court appeal.

national.text: Cronos closes European cannabis buy today — Cronos Group completed its acquisition of CanAdelaar, the largest adult-use cannabis company in the Netherlands' pilot program, establishing the top market share in Europe's largest legal cannabis market.

Compass Pathways says psilocybin launch still on for early 2027 — CEO Kabir Nath said the company is finishing its rolling FDA submission for COMP360 this quarter and plans a deliberately cautious rollout once approved.

Cannabis M&A wave keeps building post-rescheduling push — Operators like Colorado's Spherex are closing new acquisitions and investing early in integration planning as deal activity accelerates across the industry.
DEA rescheduling case paused, not dead — A DEA judge ordered the agency to respond to opponents' bid to reopen testimony, with the case formally stayed while the tribunal weighs the pending motions.

Federally funded study backs cannabis as an opioid-sparing tool — New research shows medical marijuana improves cancer-related symptoms and helps reduce opioid use, adding fresh clinical ammunition for reform advocates.
